exercises.name: Bench press
steps: Set the rack and safety arms for your reach. Lie on the bench with feet supported and upper back stable.
Grip the bar securely. Unrack with control and lower toward your chest through a comfortable range.
Press up without bouncing the bar; return it securely to the rack.
exercises.cue: Keep wrists stacked over forearms and avoid forcing a painful range.
exercises.safety: Use safety arms or a capable spotter. Do not train to failure alone under a barbell.
exercises.easier: Try a light dumbbell press or an elevated push-up.

exercises.name: Push-up
steps: Place hands on the floor or a stable elevated surface, slightly wider than shoulders.
Keep your trunk supported as you bend the elbows and lower with control.
Push the surface away and return without letting the hips sag.
exercises.cue: Move shoulders and hips together; keep breathing.
exercises.safety: Choose a stable surface and stop if you feel wrist or shoulder pain.
exercises.easier: Use a wall or higher surface to reduce the load.

exercises.name: One-arm dumbbell row
steps: Support one hand on a stable bench and hinge at the hips with the other hand holding a light dumbbell.
Pull the weight toward your hip without twisting your trunk.
Lower slowly to a comfortable arm extension and repeat on the other side.
exercises.cue: Keep your neck in line with your trunk; avoid jerking the weight.
exercises.safety: Make sure the bench is stable and the load is manageable.
exercises.easier: Use a lighter weight and more support.

exercises.name: Lat pulldown
steps: Adjust the thigh pad so you sit securely, with feet supported.
Hold the bar comfortably and pull toward the upper chest while keeping your torso steady.
Return the bar upward under control without losing your seated position.
exercises.cue: Pull in front of the head; avoid swinging your body.
exercises.safety: Do not pull behind the neck or force the shoulders beyond a comfortable range.
exercises.easier: Reduce the load or use a comfortable neutral-grip attachment.

exercises.name: Overhead press
steps: Set a light bar at upper-chest height in a rack. Grip just outside shoulder width.
Brace gently and press overhead while moving your head only enough to clear the bar.
Lower to the starting position under control.
exercises.cue: Avoid leaning back to finish the press.
exercises.safety: Use a rack and a comfortable overhead range; skip the movement if it causes pain.
exercises.easier: Try a light seated dumbbell press with support.

exercises.name: Lateral raise
steps: Stand or sit with light dumbbells at your sides and elbows softly bent.
Raise the arms out to the sides through a comfortable range, no higher than shoulder level.
Lower slowly without swinging the trunk.
exercises.cue: Start very light; keep the neck relaxed.
exercises.safety: Stop if you feel a pinching sensation in the shoulder.
exercises.easier: Use less weight and a smaller comfortable range.

exercises.name: Dumbbell curl
steps: Hold dumbbells at your sides with a comfortable grip.
Bend the elbows to curl the weights while keeping the upper arms mostly still.
Lower under control without swinging.
exercises.cue: Keep your wrists comfortable and avoid leaning backward.
exercises.safety: Reduce the load if the elbows or wrists hurt.
exercises.easier: Use lighter weights or alternate one arm at a time.

exercises.name: Triceps pushdown
steps: Attach a rope or bar to a high cable and select a light load.
Keep upper arms near your sides and extend the elbows to press down.
Let the elbows bend again slowly without letting the stack slam.
exercises.cue: Move at the elbow, not by leaning your whole body onto the attachment.
exercises.safety: Check the attachment is secure; do not force the elbows into a painful lockout.
exercises.easier: Use a lighter load and a comfortable attachment.

exercises.name: Back squat
steps: Set the rack and safety arms. Rest the bar securely on the upper back, not directly on the neck.
Unrack, take a stable stance and bend the hips and knees together.
Descend only as far as you can control, then stand with feet planted.
exercises.cue: Choose a stance and depth that suit your body; keep the load controlled.
exercises.safety: Use safety arms and seek qualified coaching before adding heavy load.
exercises.easier: Practice a bodyweight squat to a stable box.

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift
steps: Stand with light dumbbells in front of your thighs and knees slightly bent.
Push the hips back while keeping the weights close and your trunk steady.
Stop before losing control of your back position; drive the hips forward to stand.
exercises.cue: Think hips back, not weights to the floor.
exercises.safety: Avoid rounding or forcing extra depth; stop if you feel back pain.
exercises.easier: Practice the hip hinge without weight.

exercises.name: Dead bug
steps: Lie on your back with arms raised and hips and knees bent.
Keep a comfortable, stable trunk as you slowly reach one arm and the opposite leg away.
Return and alternate sides without arching your lower back.
exercises.cue: Use a small range you can control while breathing normally.
exercises.safety: Reduce the range if your lower back lifts uncomfortably or hurts.
exercises.easier: Move only the arms or tap one heel down at a time.

exercises.name: Forearm plank
steps: Place forearms on the floor with elbows under shoulders.
Extend the legs or keep knees down and gently brace the trunk.
Hold only while you can breathe and keep a controlled position, then rest.
exercises.cue: Keep hips in line with the trunk rather than chasing a longer hold.
exercises.safety: Stop for shoulder or back pain; do not hold your breath.
exercises.easier: Keep the knees down or use a stable elevated surface.

exercises.name: Brisk walk
steps: Choose a safe, even route and comfortable footwear.
Start at an easy pace, then gradually walk a little faster if comfortable.
Ease the pace before stopping.
exercises.cue: Choose a pace that lets you speak in sentences.
exercises.safety: Stop for chest pain, faintness or unusual breathlessness; seek medical help if symptoms are severe.
exercises.easier: Walk more slowly or for a shorter distance.

exercises.name: Stationary bike
steps: Adjust the seat so the knee stays slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Start with low resistance and pedal smoothly at an easy pace.
Increase effort gradually if comfortable, then ease off before stopping.
exercises.cue: Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid rocking on the saddle.
exercises.safety: Check the bike is stable; stop for pain, faintness or unusual breathlessness.
exercises.easier: Lower the resistance or shorten the session.
